cases.notes: Escaping one underscore prevents lined-fence recognition.
The < slot extends the anchor to its left; source marker is not stored in the AST.
The ^ slot extends the anchor above; a fully covered semantic row may have zero anchor cells.
Canonical ambiguous continuation chooses ^ when above and left resolve to the same anchor.
All rows must have the same logical slot width.
^ has no resolvable slot above in the first row.
< has no resolvable slot to the left in the first column.
A would own an L-shaped set of slots; span ownership must be rectangular.
The :: marker alone establishes Grid mode; a 1x1 header plus 1x1 body is valid.

cases.notes: Rowspan may exist wholly inside a multi-row Grid header.
The first body slot cannot continue a header anchor; rowspan never crosses ::.
A fenced Grid may contain at most one :: header/body separator.
When :: is present, the header row group is non-empty.
When :: is present, the body row group is non-empty.
Grid recognition ignores ::, --, and == marker-like lines inside fenced literal regions.
Equivalent escape placement is tolerated in normal mode; canonical uses the leftmost effective escape.
Equivalent escape placement is tolerated in normal mode; canonical uses the leftmost effective escape.
A normal-mode closer may be longer than its opener; canonical opener and closer are both :::.

cases.notes: A lined container may freely mix ordinary direct blocks with any number of direct fenced-container siblings.
A closer shorter than its opener does not close the container; EOF therefore leaves the fence unclosed.
Ordinary blocks directly owned by a Markanto container remain independently addressable.

A multi-line inline code span (§10.9) is a literal region for the Grid commitment scan (§2.7.7): a physical `--`/`==`/`::` line inside the still-open span is content, not a Grid marker, so this body stays ordinary fenced-container content. The `partitionBody` pre-scan tracks the open backtick run across lines — a single forward pass, no second parse. Canonical form collapses the span to one line.

A standalone block-resource opener keeps its block meaning when a `___` follows: the resource line is not a lined-container TYPE (`isLinedHeaderIntroducer` lists the block-resource and `<…` openers alongside quotes / lists / fences), so this is an ImageBlock followed by an anonymous lined container, not a typed container with an invalid TYPE.

cases.notes: A lined-container body whose last content line is directly adjacent to the closing ___ (no blank line) is still one paragraph — the boundary predicate stops at the closer, the last line is not split off.

Inside a fenced-container body a `` ```+ `` line whose remainder holds a backtick is not a code fence (§2.4) — it opens an inline code span in a body paragraph. Exercises the `codeFenceOpener` recogniser used for container-body fence detection.
